ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers taking من after كل as a relative pronoun meaning all who are in the heavens and earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r3.anchor: والأولى جعلها موصولة لأن كونها موصوفة بالنسبة إلى الموصولة قليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead calls من a descriptive indefinite after كل, by analogy with its occurrence after رب.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: من موصوفة لأنها وقعت بعد كل نكرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r5.speaker: عبد الله وابن الزبير وأبو حيوة وطلحة وأبو بحرية وابن أبي عبلة ويعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r5.claim: These readers recite إلا آت with nunation and الرحمن in the accusative; the majority read it in a genitive construction, and آتي is the predicate of كل with عبدا circumstantial.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وابن الزبير وأبو حيوة وطلحة وأبو بحرية وابن أبي عبلة ويعقوب إلا آت بالتنوين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r6.claim: Repeating الرحمن emphasizes that no one else deserves this name, since the origins and branches of blessings come from Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r6.anchor: وتكرر لفظ الرحمن تنبيها على أنه لا يستحق هذا الاسم غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r7.claim: The beings claimed as deities, including angels, Jesus, and Ezra, all come to the Merciful as obedient servants; alleged filial status cannot confer divinity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p303/r7.anchor: ومن في السموات والأرض يشمل من اتخذوه معبودا من الملائكة وعيسى وعزيرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r3.claim: Every being in the heavens and earth will come to the Merciful as a humbled, submissive servant; all creation belongs to Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r3.anchor: {إن كل من في السماوات والأرض إلا آتي الرحمن} أي إلا آتيه يوم القيامة {عبدا} ذليلا خاضعا

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r1.claim: Every being in the heavens and earth belongs to the Merciful and approaches Him as a servant in submission; one reading preserves the original form of the verb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r1.anchor: إلا وهو مملوك له يأوي إليه بالعبودية والانقياد

NAHHAS:v3p29/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p29/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p29/r3.claim: The written yāʾ in ātin reflects an original tanwīn that was omitted for ease and then annexed.
NAHHAS:v3p29/r3.anchor: آتي بالياء في الخط والأصل التنوين فحذف تخفيفا وأضيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p173/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p173/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p173/r1.claim: Ātī al-Raḥmān ʿabdan figuratively means acknowledging God and confessing His divinity; ʿabdan is a circumstantial accusative for a dependent servant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p173/r1.anchor: ومعنى { آتي الرحمن عبدا } : الإتيان المجازي ، وهو الإقرار والاعتراف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p48#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p48#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p48#2/r1.claim: Man after kull is adjectival because kull is indefinite, as in a poetic example where rabb is likewise followed by man.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p48#2/r1.anchor: {من} موصوفة لأنها وقعت بعد كل نكرة ، وقوعها بعد رب

TABRISI:19:93-96/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:93-96/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:93-96/r1.claim: Lidd means intense contentiousness; the cited verse and poem illustrate the word and its plural form.
TABRISI:19:93-96/r1.anchor: اللدد شدة الخصومة وفي التنزيل ألد الخصام

THALABI:v6p232/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p232/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v6p232/r1.claim: In a divine report, God says the servant falsely denies resurrection and slanders Him by claiming He has taken a child, then affirms divine oneness.
THALABI:v6p232/r1.anchor: أما تكذيبه إياي فأن يقول: لن يعيدنا كما بدأنا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r4.claim: Every creature in the heavens and earth will come to God on Judgment Day admitting servitude to him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r4.anchor: وهو يأتي الله سبحانه يوم القيامة مقرا له بالعبودية

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r3.claim: Every creature in heaven and earth comes to the Merciful as a servant, counted and alone on Judgment Day, as in another verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r3.anchor: ثم قال: {لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا {94} وكلهم آتيه يوم القيامة فردا {95} } [مريم: 94-95] كقوله: {ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة} [الأنعام: 94]

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Every creature in heaven and earth is God's servant on equal footing; none is His son or daughter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Each and every one is His servant equal in status. None shall be His son or daughter there.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r1.claim: All beings, including angels and humans and jinn, are God's owned servants, submitting to His decree; their coming is figurative submission.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r1.anchor: أي ما منهم أحد من الملائكة والثقلين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r2.claim: A reported alternative takes the coming bodily as arrival at the place of judgment, but al-Alusi says this is unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r2.anchor: وقيل : هو حسى والمراد إلا ماتى محل حكمه وهو ارض المحشر منقادا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r3.claim: من may be a relative pronoun, with كل denoting a generic class, as in 39:33 and a cited poetic construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r3.anchor: و ( من ) موصولة بمعنى الذي و ( كل ) تدخل عليه لأنه يراد منه الجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r4.claim: The relative-pronoun analysis is preferred in al-Bahr because the use of من as a descriptor is comparatively rare.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r4.anchor: ورجح في البحر الأول بأن مجيئها موصوفة بالنسبة إلى مجيئها موصولة قليل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r5.claim: Abdullah, Ibn al-Zubayr, Abu Haywa, Talha, Abu Bahriya, Ibn Abi Abla, and Yaqub read مات with nunation and الرحمن in the accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وابن الزبير وابو حيوة وطلحة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r6.claim: In both readings, عبدا is accusative as a circumstantial accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r6.anchor: + ونصب ( عبدا ) في القراءتين على الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r7.claim: The verse supports the legal view that a father cannot own his son and that a son is emancipated if his father acquires him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p142/r7.anchor: واستدل بالاية على أن الوالد لا يملك ولده وانه يعتق عليه إذا ملكه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r21.claim: All who come to the Merciful do so as poor, humbled servants, wholly stripped of selfhood.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r21.anchor: فقيرا ذليلا منقادا مسلوب الأنانية بالكلية

BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r1.claim: Every being in heaven and earth, including angels and both kinds of rational creatures, comes as God’s owned servant, taking refuge in Him through submission.
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r1.anchor: أي : ما منهم أحد من الملائكة والثقلين فإن بمعنى النفي كما ولك مبتدأ خبره آتى ومن موصوفة لأنها وقعت بعد كل نكرة

BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r2.speaker: العيون
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r2.claim: Al-Uyun says all creatures will come humbled before the Merciful, acknowledging servitude like angels, Jesus, and Ezra; therefore none can be His child.
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r2.anchor: وفي "العيون" : سيأتي جميع الخلائق يوم القيامة إلى الرحمن خاضعا ذليلا مقرا بالعبودية

BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r3.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says the best approach to God is steadfast servanthood and expressed need: the former sustains service and the latter sustained turning, pleading, and supplication.
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق رحمه الله : ما تقرب أحد إلى ربه بشيء ازين عليه من ملازمة العبودية

BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r4.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r4.claim: Hafiz’s Persian verse depicts the speaker arriving poor and wounded at God’s court, with no support other than prayer for mercy.
BURSEVI:v5p275#2/r4.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
فقير وخسته بدركاهت آمدم رحمى

QASHANI:19:93-95/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:93-95/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:93-95/r1.claim: All in heaven and earth come as servants because possible beings have no existence or perfection apart from divine effusion through Rahman; they remain governed and compelled under His dominion.
QASHANI:19:93-95/r1.anchor: لكونهم في حيز الإمكان ومكمن العدم لا وجود لهم ولا كمال إلا به، أفاض باسم الرحمن وجوداتهم وكمالاتهم

QASHANI:19:93-95/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:93-95/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:93-95/r2.claim: Their primordial readiness worships God so they may exist; after existence they owe worship by fulfilling the rights of His gifts to become complete.
QASHANI:19:93-95/r2.anchor: فلو لم يعبدوه حق عبادته باستعدادات أعيانهم في العدم لما وجدوا، ولو لم يعبدوه بعد الوجوه بالقيام بحقوق نعمه التي أنعمها عليهم لما كملوا،

BIQAI-FULL:v4p557/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p557/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p557/r10.claim: God needs no child and cannot have one: offspring requires shared kind, but nothing shares the absolute Creator’s kind; every heavenly and earthly being comes to him as a subdued servant, which opposes sonship and partnership.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p557/r10.anchor: مسخرا مقهورا خائفا راجيا , فكيف يكون العبد ابنا أو شريكا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p557/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p557/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p557/r11.claim: The verse also supports the rule that a parent and child are both freed if purchased.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p557/r11.anchor: فهي من الدليل على عتق الولد والوالد إذا اشتريا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r4.claim: Inna is negative, equivalent to mā; the common reading annexes “coming” to the Merciful.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r4.anchor: وقوله إن كل من في السماوات الآية إن نافية بمعنى ما، وقرأ الجمهور «آتي الرحمن» بالإضافة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r5.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r5.claim: Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif reads ātin with tanwīn and the following noun in the accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r5.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف «آت الرحمن» بتنوين «آت» والنصب في النون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads lammā atā al-Raḥmān.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r7.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r7.claim: Some infer that a child cannot be a servant; the author calls this inference remote.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r7.anchor: واستدل بعض الناس بهذه الآية على أن الولد لا يكون عبدا وهذا انتزاع بعيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r8.claim: ʿAbdan is an accusative of state.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r9.claim: God encompasses and knows His servants; enumeration is stated and restated in different words, while ʿaddan emphasizes the action.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r9.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى عن إحاطته ومعرفته بعبيده فذكر الإحصاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r10.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads “He wrote them down and counted them.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r11.speaker: أبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r11.claim: Ubayy's codex reads “He counted them and enumerated them completely.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r11.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي «لقد أحصاهم فأجملهم عددا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r12.claim: Arriving alone conveys little support or strength, with no protector from God's will.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r12.anchor: وقوله فردا يتضمن معنى قلة النصر والحول والقوة لا مجير له مما يريد الله به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r22.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r22.claim: The verse may connect to the preceding account of everyone coming as servant and alone: God comforts believers through love shown in honor, gifts, and signs of forgiveness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p34/r22.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الآية متصلة بما قبلها في المعنى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p265#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p265#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p265#3/r1.claim: Everyone in heaven and earth will come to God on Judgment Day as a humble servant, including Jesus, Ezra, and the angels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p265#3/r1.anchor: يوم القيامة عبدا ذليلا خاضعا والمعنى أن عيسى وعزيرا والملائكة عبيد له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p265#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p265#3/r2.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p265#3/r2.claim: Abu Yaʿla infers that a parent who buys his own child no longer owns him, since purchase emancipates him: sonship and enslavement cannot coexist.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p265#3/r2.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أن الوالد إذا اشترى ولده لم يبق ملكه عليه وإنما يعتق بنفس الشراء

SULAMI:v1p433#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p433#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v1p433#2/r1.claim: The finest approach to God is constant servanthood and confessed need: servanthood sustains service, and need sustains refuge and humble pleading.
SULAMI:v1p433#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : ما تقرب أحد إلى ربه بشيء أزين عليه من ملازمة العبودية وإظهار الافتقار لأن ملازمة العبودية تورث دوام الخدمة

SULAMI:v1p433#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p433#2/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
SULAMI:v1p433#2/r2.claim: The one who comes to the Merciful as a servant is poor and humbled by his own qualities, or noble by pointing through the qualities of the Real.
SULAMI:v1p433#2/r2.anchor: عن علي بن موسى الرضا عن أبيه عن جعفر بن محمد في قوله ﴿ إلا آتي الرحمن عبدا ﴾ قال : فقيرا ذليلا بأوصافه أو عزيزا دالا بأوصاف الحق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267/r2.claim: God has counted every creature, male and female, young and old, from creation until Resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267/r2.anchor: أي: قد علم عددهم منذ خلقهم إلى يوم القيامة، ذكرهم وأنثاهم وصغيرهم وكبيرهم

JISHUMI:v6p4621/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r6.claim: Servanthood and sonship cannot coexist; if a man owned his son, the son would be emancipated.
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن العبودية والبنوة لا يجتمعان، فدل أنه إذا ملك ابنه عتق عليه

JISHUMI:v6p4621/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r7.claim: Every being coming to God as a servant negates divine offspring, since God is not a body and offspring is a property of bodies.
JISHUMI:v6p4621/r7.anchor: لأنه يدل أنه ليس بجسم والولد من خصائص الأجسام

MUQATIL:19:93-95/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:93-95/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:93-95/r1.claim: All in the heavens and earth, including angels, ʿUzayr, Jesus, Mary, and others, come to the Merciful as servants who acknowledge servitude to him.
MUQATIL:19:93-95/r1.anchor: من الملائكة وغيرهم، وعزير، وعيسى، ومريم وغيرهم، فهؤلاء في الأرض

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r1.claim: إن كل من is an indefinite noun described by the following phrase; its predicate is إلا آتي الرحمن. The singular participle and pronoun agree with the lexical form of كل; it is an active participle in future sense.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r1.anchor: نكرة موصوفة صفتها ﴿ في السماوات والأرض ﴾ وخبر كل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r2.claim: عبدا is a circumstantial accusative meaning submissive, lowly, and obedient; all angels and humans come before God on Judgment Day admitting servitude.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r2.anchor: حال أي خاضعا ذليلا منقادا والمعنى ما كل من في السموات والأرض من الملائكة والناس الا هو يأتي الله يوم القيامة مقرا بالعبودية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r3.claim: Servitude and sonship are incompatible: all are attributed to God as servants; even ownership of one's child would emancipate the child, so some cannot be children while others are servants.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r3.anchor: والعبودية والبنوة تتنافيان حتى لوم ملك الأب ابنه يعتق عليه ونسبه الجميع اليه نسبة العبد إلى المولى فكيف يكون البعض ولدا والبعض عبدا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r4.claim: Ibn Masud reads آت الرحمن in its original form before annexation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49/r4.anchor: وقرا ابن مسعود آت الرحمن على اصله قبل الإضافة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r1.claim: “In” is negative: everyone in heaven and earth will come on Judgment Day acknowledging God’s lordship in submission, as in 27:87; all are His servants, so none can be His child.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r1.anchor: أي ما كل من في السموات والأرض إلا وهو يأتي يوم القيامة مقرا له بالعبودية

QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r2.claim: “Ātī” is written with yāʾ; its original tanwīn is dropped for ease and the form is annexed.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r2.anchor: و«آتي» بالياء في الخط، والأصل التنوين فحذف استخفافا وأضيف

QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r3.claim: The verse proves a parent cannot own a child: God contrasts sonship with servitude, which cannot coexist; if a father cannot own his son, the son cannot own his father all the more.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r3.anchor: وقد أبان الله تعالى المنافاة بين الأولاد والملك

QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r4.claim: The sound Muslim report says a child cannot repay a parent except by finding the parent enslaved, buying him, and freeing him.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r4.anchor: لا يجزي ولد والدا إلا أن يجده مملوكا فيشتريه فيعتقه

QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r5.speaker: إسحاق بن راهويه
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r5.claim: Isḥāq ibn Rāhwayh interprets emancipation of a share in a slave as referring only to male slaves, so freeing a share in a female would not complete emancipation.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r5.anchor: ذهب إسحاق بن راهويه في تأويل قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r6.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r6.claim: The majority reject Isḥāq’s distinction and include male and female slaves, since “ʿabd” is generic and this verse encompasses both.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r6.anchor: وهو على خلاف ما ذهب إليه الجمهور من السلف ومن بعدهم

QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r7.claim: A divine saying transmitted by al-Bukhārī through Abū Hurayra says Adam’s son falsely denies resurrection and insults God by claiming He has a child, though He is One and has no offspring or equal.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93/r7.anchor: كذبني ابن آدم ولم يكن له ذلك وشتمني ولم يكن له ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:19:93#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93#2/r1.claim: The discussion had appeared under al-Baqara and elsewhere; repeating it here is appropriate.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:93#2/r1.anchor: وقد تقدم في «البقرة» وغيرها وإعادته في مثل هذا الموضع حسن جدا

RAZI-FULL:v21p217#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p217#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p217#2/r8.claim: Every worshipped being in heaven and earth, including angels and people, returns to God as a submissive, humble servant who hopes in Him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p217#2/r8.anchor: والمراد أنه ما من معبود لهم في السموات والأرض من الملائكة والناس إلا وهو يأتي

RAZI-FULL:v21p217#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p217#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p217#2/r9.claim: Some restrict the statement about every being coming as a servant to the Day of Judgment; Razi prefers the unrestricted reading because it needs no restriction.
RAZI-FULL:v21p217#2/r9.anchor: ومنهم من حمله على يوم القيامة خاصة والأول أولى لأنه لا تخصيص فيه

STUDYQURAN:19:93/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:93/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:93/r1.claim: All created beings being servants means God is the Lord of all things and they are servants in relation to Him.
STUDYQURAN:19:93/r1.anchor: which are therefore servants in relation to Him.

STUDYQURAN:19:93/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:93/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:93/r2.claim: The angels, humans, and jinn ultimately worship God, as 51:56 says of jinn and humankind.
STUDYQURAN:19:93/r2.anchor: they all, ultimately, worship Him; cf. 51:56: I did not create jinn and mankind, save to worship Me.

TAB-FULL:v15p639#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p639#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p639#2/r5.claim: All angels, humans, and jinn will come to God on Judgment Day as His humbled servants, affirming their servitude and having no kinship with Him.
TAB-FULL:v15p639#2/r5.anchor: يقول: إلا يأتي ربه يوم القيامة عبدا له، ذليلا خاضعا، مقرا له بالعبودية، لا نسب بينه وبينه.

TAB-FULL:v15p639#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p639#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p639#2/r6.claim: Ātī is an active participle from the verb ataytuhu, meaning I came to him.
TAB-FULL:v15p639#2/r6.anchor: وقوله: {آتي الرحمن} [مريم: 93] إنما هو فاعل من أتيته، فأنا آتيه

TABATABAI:19:92-93/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r1.claim: Every being’s coming as God’s servant means appearing before Him in complete ownership: no creature independently owns benefit, harm, death, life, or resurrection, and this servitude holds throughout existence.
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r1.anchor: المراد بإتيان كل منهم عبدا له توجه الكل إليه ومثوله بين يديه في صفة المملوكية المحضة فكل منهم مملوك له لا يملك لنفسه نفعا ولا ضرا ولا موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا

TABATABAI:19:92-93/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r2.claim: Unlike the verse about coming alone at Judgment, this verse does not specify Judgment Day because the state of servitude is already actual and continuous.
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r2.anchor: ولذا لم يقيد الإتيان في الآية بالقيامة بخلاف ما في الآية الرابعة

TABATABAI:19:92-93/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r5.claim: The passage offers one argument against divine offspring: every being is wholly owned, counted, assigned a role, and finally appears alone; such need and poverty cannot coexist with divinity or derivation from God’s essence.
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r5.anchor: وإذا كان هذا حال كل من في السماوات والأرض فكيف يمكن أن يكون بعضهم ولدا لله واجدا لحقيقة اللاهوت مشتقا من جوهرتها، وكيف تجتمع الألوهية والفقر

TABATABAI:19:92-93/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r6.claim: Believers in a creator, whether monotheists or polytheists, agree that all existence ends with one creator; they differ over multiple objects of worship and delegated lords or managers.
TABATABAI:19:92-93/r6.anchor: فمما لا يرتاب فيه مثبتو الصانع سواء في ذلك الموحدون والمشركون وإنما الاختلاف في كثرة المعبود ووحدته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r4.claim: Those in heaven are angels and those on earth are creatures; each comes to God as a lowly, submissive servant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: {إن كل} أي: ما كل {من في السماوات} من فيها من الملائكة {الأرض} من فيها من الخلق {إلا آتي الرحمن} إلا يأتيه يوم {عبدا} ذليلا خاضعا منقادا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r5.claim: All creation are God’s servants, including Jesus and ʿUzayr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r5.anchor: يعني: أن الخلق عبيده، وأن عيسى وعزيرا من جملة العبيد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r6.claim: The word ʿabdan is accusative as a circumstantial expression (ḥāl).
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p338#2/r6.anchor: انتصب {عبدا} على الحال {لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا} أي: عرف عددهم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:93/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:93/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:93/r1.claim: God created the heavens, earth, and all their inhabitants, including angels, jinn, and humans; they are servants, not deities, and obey and worship Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:93/r1.anchor: Gökler, yer, bunların içinde bulunan melek, cin, insan vb. ne varsa hepsini Allah yaratmıştır; onlar tanrı değil Allah’ın kullarıdır

SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء والزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r1.claim: They take من في السماوات as an indefinite noun qualified by the following prepositional phrase; their wording appears to exclude other parses.
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r1.anchor: يجوز في " من " أن تكون نكرة موصوفة، وصفتها الجار بعدها.

SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r2.claim: من may instead be relative, with كل applying to a generic relative noun; it must be universal rather than one known person.
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون موصولة. قال الشيخ: " أي: ما كل الذي في السماوات،

SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r3.claim: The poetic كل الذي حملتني supports the relative analysis; the relative must be interpreted universally for كل to be annexed to it.

SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r4.claim: آتي الرحمن is the predicate of كل, singular by its form; plural would also be possible when agreement follows meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r4.anchor: و { آتي الرحمن } خبر " كل " جعل مفردا حملا على لفظها ولو جمع لجاز وقد تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r5.speaker: السهيلي
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r5.claim: Al-Suhayli says clause-initial كل annexed to a definite should take a singular predicate, understood as كل واحد; the Sheikh requires Arabic attestation for plural agreement.
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r5.anchor: وقد تكلم السهيلي في ذلك فقال:

SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r6.claim: The author corrects the terminology: singular agreement follows the word's form, while plural follows meaning; Quranic plural examples have كل unannexed.
SAMIN-DURR:19:95/r6.anchor: بل ذلك حمل على اللفظ، الجمع هو الحمل على المعنى.

SAMIN-DURR:19:93/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:93/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير وأبو حيوة وطلحة
SAMIN-DURR:19:93/r1.claim: They and others read آتي with tanwin and الرحمن in the accusative; the majority use annexation.
SAMIN-DURR:19:93/r1.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن الزبير وأبو حيوة وطلحة وجماعة بتنوينه ونصب " الرحمن ".

SAMIN-DURR:19:93/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:93/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:93/r2.claim: عبدا and فردا are circumstantial accusatives.
SAMIN-DURR:19:93/r2.anchor: وانتصب " عبدا " و " فردا " على الحال.

ASAD-NOTES:19:93#n78/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:93#n78/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:93#n78/r1.claim: All beings, human and angelic, are created, share none of God's divinity, and submit to His will consciously or unconsciously.
ASAD-NOTES:19:93#n78/r1.anchor: all of them - whether men or angels - are but created beings, having no share whatever in His divinity, and all of them submit, consciously or unconsciously, to His will

BURHAN:v4p215/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p215/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p215/r8.claim: A second إن functions like ما and enters nominal clauses in an exceptive construction, as in 19:93 and the listed parallel statements.
BURHAN:v4p215/r8.anchor: الثاني بمنزلة لا وتدخل على الجملة الاسمية

BURHAN:v2p3/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p3/r1.speaker: الغزالي
BURHAN:v2p3/r1.claim: Al-Ghazali and others, followed by al-Razi, give five hundred as the number of legal verses; the author says they likely mean explicit rulings, since stories and parables also yield many rulings, and directs readers to Ibn Abd al-Salam.
BURHAN:v2p3/r1.anchor: ثم قيل إن آيات الأحكام خمسمائة آية وهذا ذكره الغزالي وغيره

BURHAN:v2p3/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p3/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p3/r2.claim: Legal verses divide into explicit rulings and rulings derived by inference; derived rulings in turn come either from one verse alone or by joining multiple verses.
BURHAN:v2p3/r2.anchor: ثم هو قسمان أحدهما ما صرح به في الأحكام

BURHAN:v2p3/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p3/r5.speaker: الشافعي
BURHAN:v2p3/r5.claim: Al-Shafi‘i infers that ownership automatically frees an ascendant or descendant: servitude is placed opposite parentage, so the two statuses cannot coexist.
BURHAN:v2p3/r5.anchor: واستنباطه عتق الأصل والفرع بمجرد الملك

BURHAN:v4p321/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p321/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p321/r1.claim: With من understood as a relative pronoun, the verse combines agreement with كل’s singular form and plural meaning; if من is an indefinite descriptor, the example belongs to the prior category.
BURHAN:v4p321/r1.anchor: وقد اجتمع مراعاة اللفظ والمعنى في قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v4p321/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p321/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p321/r2.claim: When كل is cut off from an expressed genitive, it can agree either with its singular form or its collective meaning; the source gives both singular and plural examples.
BURHAN:v4p321/r2.anchor: الثالث إن تقطع عن الإضافة لفظا فيجوز مراعاة لفظها ومراعاة معناها

BURHAN:v4p321/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p321/r3.speaker: أبو الفتح
BURHAN:v4p321/r3.claim: Abu al-Fath explains mixed singular and plural agreement by the word’s singular form and collective meaning, with an omitted plural genitive sometimes reflected in agreement and sometimes not.
BURHAN:v4p321/r3.anchor: قال أبو الفتح وعلته إن أحد الجمعين عندهم كان عن صاحبه

BURHAN:v4p321/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p321/r6.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v4p321/r6.claim: Al-Suhayli says a detached كل should take a plural predicate because it means a group; for the cited singular predicates, he invokes contextual clues favoring that wording.
BURHAN:v4p321/r6.anchor: وقال السهيلي السهيلي في نتاج الفكر

BURHAN:v1p13/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p13/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p13/r1.claim: Tafsir is the knowledge of understanding God’s revealed Book, explaining its meanings, and deriving its rulings and wisdom; it draws on language, grammar, morphology, rhetoric, legal theory, and readings, and requires knowledge of revelation contexts and abrogation.
BURHAN:v1p13/r1.anchor: التفسير علم يعرف به فهم كتاب الله المنزل على نبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURHAN:v1p13/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p13/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p13/r2.claim: Exegetical works reflect their authors’ strongest fields: al-Zajjaj and al-Wahidi emphasize rare vocabulary, al-Tha‘labi stories, al-Zamakhshari rhetoric, and Fakhr al-Din kalam and rational disciplines.
BURHAN:v1p13/r2.anchor: فالزجاج والواحدى في البسيط يغلب عليهما الغريب والثعلبى يغلب عليه القصص

BURHAN:v1p13/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p13/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p13/r3.claim: Although God addressed people in a language they understand and revealed each book in its people’s language, commentary is needed when concise expression hides subtle meaning, premises are omitted, wording permits several readings, or a human text contains errors or omissions.
BURHAN:v1p13/r3.anchor: وإنما احتيج إلى الشروح لأمور ثلاثة أحدها كمال فضيلة المصنف

BURHAN:v1p13/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p13/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p13/r4.claim: The Qur’an came in clear Arabic among the most eloquent Arabs; they knew its surface meanings and rulings, while subtler meanings emerged through study and, often, questions to the Prophet.
BURHAN:v1p13/r4.anchor: إن القرآن إنما أنزل بلسان عربى مبين في زمن أفصح العرب

ITQAN:v2p492#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r4.claim: When kull is annexed to a definite, its agreement can follow its singular masculine form or its collective meaning; both occur across this verse and the next clause.
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r4.anchor: أو إلى معرف جاز مراعاة لفظها في الإفراد والتذكير ومراعاة معناها وقد اجتمعا

ITQAN:v2p492#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r5.claim: The same alternatives of agreement apply when kull stands without annexation, as the cited examples show.
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r5.anchor: أو قطعت فكذلك نحو ﴿ قل كل يعمل على شاكلته ﴾

ITQAN:v4p462#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r1.claim: Commentaries are needed because concise wording can hide fine meanings, a writer can omit assumed conditions, and words can bear competing senses or contain errors and omissions.
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r1.anchor: وإنما احتيج إلى الشروح لأمور ثلاثة

ITQAN:v4p462#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r2.claim: The Qur’an came in Arabic among eloquent Arabs who knew its apparent wording and rulings; subtle meanings often emerged through inquiry and asking the Prophet.
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r2.anchor: وكانوا يعلمون ظواهره وأحكامه أما دقائق باطنه فإنما كان يظهر لهم بعد البحث والنظر

ITQAN:v4p462#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r4.claim: Later Muslims need interpretation even more than the first Arabs, because they lack untrained command of Arabic and cannot independently discern the rulings of surface wording.
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r4.anchor: فنحن أشد الناس احتياجا إلى التفسير

ITQAN:v4p462#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r5.claim: Tafsir works both by expanding concise expressions and by weighing one possible meaning against another.
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r5.anchor: بسط الألفاظ الوجيزة وكشف معانيها وبعضه من قبل ترجيح بعض الاحتمالات على بعض

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r1.claim: Fronted مثل need not refer to a second person: it can mean that anyone matching the addressee in quality would naturally act or refrain as described.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r1.anchor: ومما يرى تقديم الاسم فيه كاللازم ' مثل ' و ' غير ' في نحو قوله

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r2.claim: The reply to al-Ḥajjāj’s threat exploits مثل الأمير to comment on what an emir’s rank or customary conduct entails, not to refer to another person.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r2.anchor: فقال على سبيل المغالطة : ومثل الأمير يحمل على الأدهم والأشهب .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r3.claim: Likewise, غيري can mean I am not among those who are deceived or ungrateful; it does not necessarily identify and disparage another person.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r3.anchor: على معنى أني لا أفعله ، لا أن يومىء ' بغير ' إلى إنسان فيخبر عنه بأن يفعل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r4.claim: Abū Tammām’s غيري verse denies that he is ungrateful and base; Jurjānī says it cannot be an accusation that another poet committed the offense.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r4.anchor: وكذلك لم يرد أبو تمام بقوله ، + الوافر + :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r5.claim: Using مثل and غير this way is rooted in ordinary instinct and established usage.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p116/r5.anchor: واستعمال ' مثل ' و ' غير ' على هذا السبيل شيء مركوز في الطباع

DAMGHANI:v1p15/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p15/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p15/r2.claim: Atā can mean acknowledge and submit: every creature comes to the Merciful acknowledging servitude.
DAMGHANI:v1p15/r2.anchor: الإتيان الإقرار والطاعة قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r1.claim: Ityān is the verbal noun of atā, meaning to come; ātā with a long vowel means to give, and the camel’s form istāʾtat describes seeking a mate.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r1.anchor: الإتيان : مصدر قولك : أتى ، يأتي ، إتيانا ، وهو بمعنى : جاء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r8.claim: A seventh sense is acknowledgment: every being comes to the Merciful admitting servitude to Him.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p165/r8.anchor: والسابع : الإقرار ومنه قوله تعالى في مريم :

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r1.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar did not know Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt’s verse likening earth to a female for rain; later interpreters explain rain makes the earth bear vegetation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r1.anchor: وحدثني أبو حاتم ، عن الأصمعي أنه قال

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r2.claim: The verse’s imagery treats earth as female and rain as male, which fertilizes it; the same pairing is applied to firesticks, whose spark is their offspring.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r2.anchor: معناه: أن الله جعل الأرض كالأنثى للماء، وجل الماء كالذكر للأرض، فإذا مطرت أنبتت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r3.claim: مسفد means mated: the male si fada the female, and God caused him to mate, parallel to nakaha/ankahahu.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r3.anchor: و (مسفد) بمعنى: منكح. تقول: سفد الذكر الأنثى، والله أسفده

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r4.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r4.claim: In Dhu al-Rumma’s parallel verse, السقط means fire, the father is the upper firestick, and the mother is the lower firestick.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r5.claim: A second Umayya poem was transmitted as عسل ما, but the author says it should read سلع ما; al-Salʿ and al-ʿUshr are trees used in rain-making rites by tying and burning them on cows’ tails.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r5.anchor: هكذا رواه عسل ما وإنما هو: سلع ما. ومعنى البيت: أنهم كانوا يستمطرون بالسلع والعشر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r6.claim: وعالت البيقورا means a drought year burdened the cows with the ritual branches and fire; al-ʿāʾil means poor, and a second poet’s verse supports the corrected reading سلع.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r7.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r7.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī said the learned had disappeared who could explain Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse about سلكى and مخلوجة.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r7.anchor: وحدثني أيضا أبو حاتم، عن الأصمعي، أنه قال

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r8.claim: The source continues al-Aṣmaʿī’s report, saying likewise that no one remained who understood al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza’s verse about those who struck the ʿayr.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p62/r8.anchor: وقال مثل ذلك في بيت الحارث بن حلزة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r1.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī reads سلكى as a straight stab and مخلوجة as one veering right or left, like two arrows that do not land alike.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r1.anchor: وفسره الأصمعي فقال: أراد نطعنهم طعنة سلكى، أي مستوية

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r2.speaker: زيد بن كثوة العنبري
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r2.claim: Zayd says people misquote the line: it is كر كلامين على نابل, two stabs delivered without pause, like telling an archer twice to shoot; he prefers this sense.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r2.anchor: وقال الزيادي : كان زيد بن كثوة العنبري يقول: الناس يغلطون في لفظ هذا البيت ومعناه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r3.speaker: بعضهم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r3.claim: One view makes العير a tent peg, named for its protrusion like the raised middle of an arrowhead; the line blames the group for every tent-dweller’s offense.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r3.anchor: فكان بعضهم يجعله الوتد، سماه عيرا لنتوئه مثل عير نصل السهم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r4.claim: Another view identifies العير with Kulaib Waʾil, the chief, deriving the title from the onager as the largest wild animal.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو كليب وائل، والعير: سيد القوم، سمي بذلك لأن العير أكبر الوحش

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r5.claim: The Prophet told Abu Sufyan, «كل الصيد في جوف العير», a report used to support العير as the greatest beast.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، لأبي سفيان

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r6.speaker: آخر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r6.claim: A further view makes العير a mountain near Medina and invokes the Prophet’s prohibition of the area between ʿAyr and Thawr; the line implicates anyone reaching that place.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r6.anchor: وقال آخر: العير جبل بالمدينة، ومنه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حرم ما بين عير إلى ثور

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r7.speaker: آخر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes العير literally as a donkey: the group is blamed for the offenses of everyone who drives one.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r7.anchor: وقال آخر: هو الحمار نفسه، يريد أنفسهم يضيفون إلينا ذنوب كل من ساق حمارا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba sums up the views: the speakers are saddled with everyone’s sins and treated as their allies.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r8.anchor: ومعنى هذا كله: أنهم يلزموننا بذنوب الناس جميعا، ويجعلوننا أولياءهم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r9.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r9.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī cannot determine two phrases by Ruʾba: the line about الأهيغ seems to imply water, and he also does not know كأنه حامل جنب أخذعا.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r9.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: لا أدري ما معنى قول رؤبة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r10.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r10.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says منغمس في الأهيغين means absorbed in eating and sex; the two الأطيبان likewise mean food and sex.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r10.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي : يقال: فلان منغمس في الأهيغين، يراد: الأكل والنكاح

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r11.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r11.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī explains that a sword blow left the bull’s side hanging as it leaned; خذع means inclination.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p64/r11.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: أراد: كأنه ضرب بالسيف ضربة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r10.claim: The forced servitude of all creatures to God is universal and gives no one a distinction in merit.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r10.anchor: العبودية القسرية وهي التي يشترك فيها كل الخلق كافرهم ومؤمنهم وذلك نحو قوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p43/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p43/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p43/r2.claim: The author distinguishes compulsory servitude, which every creature has whether willing or not, from chosen servitude, the highest station of the righteous.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p43/r2.anchor: والعبودية نوعان: قسرية واختيارية، فالعبودية القسرية تتحقق شاء أم أبى

MUALLAQAT:v1p189#4/r1.author: al-Zawzanī
MUALLAQAT:v1p189#4/r1.speaker: author
MUALLAQAT:v1p189#4/r1.claim: Al-Zawzanī explains the line as a cow fearing that either space between her legs may be the locus of danger, so she cannot tell which way to flee.
MUALLAQAT:v1p189#4/r1.anchor: يقول: فغدت البقرة وهي تحسب أن كلا فرجيها مولى المخافة، أي موضعها وصاحبها

MUALLAQAT:v1p189#4/r2.author: al-Zawzanī
MUALLAQAT:v1p189#4/r2.speaker: author
MUALLAQAT:v1p189#4/r2.claim: Al-Zawzanī says كلا is singular in form but dual in sense, while كل is singular in form despite its collective sense; 19:93 illustrates agreement by form, alongside 18:33 and 27:87 as contrasts.
MUALLAQAT:v1p189#4/r2.anchor: ونظير كلا وكلتا في هذين الحكمين كل؛ لأنه مفرد اللفظ وإن كان معناه جمعا

MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r1.author: al-Zawzanī
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r1.speaker: author
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r1.claim: The poet reports a sweeping claim that everyone who performs the act under discussion is their ally, then says he is their ally; al-Zawzanī says the line's ending has the same sense under every reading of العير.
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r1.anchor: قوله: وأنا الولاء، أي أصحاب ولائهم، فحذف المضاف، ثم إن فسر العير بالسيد

MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r2.author: al-Zawzanī
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r2.speaker: author
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r2.claim: If العير means a lord, the claim is that all who approve killing Kalib b. Wa'il are their cousins and the blood-feuds attach to the poet's group as allies.
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r2.anchor: ثم إن فسر العير بالسيد كان تحرير المعنى: زعم الأراقم أن كل من يرضى بقتل كليب وائل بنو أعمامنا

MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r3.author: al-Zawzanī
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r3.speaker: author
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r3.claim: If العير means a wild ass, all hunters of wild asses are called their allies, extending the guilt of a particular group to the public.
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r3.anchor: وإن فسر بالحمار كان المعنى: أنهم زعموا أن كل من صاد حمر الوحش موالينا

MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r4.author: al-Zawzanī
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r4.speaker: author
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r4.claim: If العير means a tent peg, everyone who pitches tents is called their ally, extending one group's guilt to the Arabs at large.
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r4.anchor: وإن فسر بالوتد كان المعنى: زعموا أن كل من ضرب الخيام وطنبها بأوتادها موالينا

MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r5.author: al-Zawzanī
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r5.speaker: author
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r5.claim: If العير means a mote, everyone who stirs motes aside to clear water is called their ally.
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r5.anchor: وإن فسر بالقذى كان المعنى: زعموا أن كل من ضرب القذى ليتنحي فيصفوا الماء موالينا

MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r6.author: al-Zawzanī
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r6.speaker: author
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r6.claim: If العير means a particular mountain, everyone who reaches that mountain is called their ally.
MUALLAQAT:v1p272#5/r6.anchor: وإن فسر بالجبل المعين كان المعنى: زعموا أن كل من صار إلى هذا الجبل موال لنا

NASHR:v1p17/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p17/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p17/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jazari rejects a reading that cannot be attributed to reliable transmission because it has no valid Arabic basis, and rejects one transmitted only by an unreliable source even more strongly; he found no Hamza reading of the disputed kind in either sound or weak routes.
NASHR:v1p17/r1.anchor: فهو مما لا يقبل، إذ لا وجه له،

NASHR:v1p17/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p17/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p17/r2.claim: A reading that matches Arabic and the written muṣḥaf but has no transmission is even more clearly forbidden; its proponent commits a grave sin. Ibn Miqsam was reported to permit it.
NASHR:v1p17/r2.anchor: ما وافق العربية والرسم ولم ينقل البتة، فهذا رده أحق

NASHR:v1p17/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p17/r3.speaker: أبو طاهر بن أبي هاشم
NASHR:v1p17/r3.claim: Abu Tahir quotes a contemporary who claimed that any Arabic form conforming to the muṣḥaf could be recited in prayer; he calls this an innovation that strays from the right path.
NASHR:v1p17/r3.anchor: فزعم أن كل من صح عنده وجه في العربية بحرف

NASHR:v1p17/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p17/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الخطيب
NASHR:v1p17/r4.claim: Al-Khatib reports that a Baghdad gathering of jurists and Qur'an readers unanimously barred the practice, ordered the man flogged, and recorded his repentance.
NASHR:v1p17/r4.anchor: وأجمعوا على منعه، وأوقف للضرب فتاب ورجع

NASHR:v1p17/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p17/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وزيد بن ثابت وابن المنكدر وعروة بن الزبير وعمر بن عبد العزيز وعامر الشعبي
NASHR:v1p17/r5.claim: These early authorities say recitation is received as a transmitted Sunnah from one generation to the next, so people must read as they were taught.
NASHR:v1p17/r5.anchor: القراءة سنة يأخذها الآخر عن الأول فاقرءوا كما علمتموه

NASHR:v1p17/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p17/r6.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v1p17/r6.claim: Nafi and Abu Amr said that, if they were free to depart from their received transmission, they would recite certain alternative forms; their statement illustrates their restraint.
NASHR:v1p17/r6.anchor: كنافع وأبي عمرو يقول: لولا أنه ليس لي أن أقرأ

NASHR:v1p17/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p17/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p17/r7.claim: Analogy grounded in an established consensus or a reliable principle may be used when explicit transmission is absent and performance is unclear, especially when it helps resolve a necessary question; Ibn al-Jazari says this may not technically be qiyas.
NASHR:v1p17/r7.anchor: إذا كان القياس على إجماع انعقد، أو عن أصل يعتمد

AZRAQI:v1p179/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p179/r1.speaker: أبو صالح مولى أم هاني
AZRAQI:v1p179/r1.claim: The passage enumerates Quraysh and a broad set of Arab groups, including Kināna, Khuzāʿa, Aws and Khazraj, Thaqīf, Ghatafān, ʿAdwān, and Quḍāʿa.
AZRAQI:v1p179/r1.anchor: عن أبي صالح مولى أم هاني قريش وكل من ولدت من العرب وكنانة وخزاعة والأوس والخزرج

AZRAQI:v1p179/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p179/r2.speaker: قريش
AZRAQI:v1p179/r2.claim: When Quraysh married a woman from another Arab group, they stipulated that any children she bore would be Ahmasī and follow Quraysh's religion.
AZRAQI:v1p179/r2.anchor: وكانت قريش إذا أنكحوا عربيا إمرأة منهم اشترطوا عليه أن كل من ولدت له فهو أحمسي علي دينهم

AZRAQI:v1p179/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p179/r3.speaker: قريش
AZRAQI:v1p179/r3.claim: As an example, Quraysh married al-Adram Taim ibn Ghalib to Majd, daughter of Taim Rabīʿa ibn ʿĀmir, on the condition that their children follow Quraysh's Ahmasī practice.
AZRAQI:v1p179/r3.anchor: وزوج الأدرم تيم بن غالب بن فهر بن مالك بن النضر بن كنانة إبنه مجدا إبنة تيم ربيعة بن عامر

AZRAQI:v1p179/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p179/r4.speaker: لبيد بن ربيعة بن جعفر الكلابي
AZRAQI:v1p179/r4.claim: The source cites Labīd's verse naming Majd, Numayr, and the tribes of Hilāl in a line about his people and their watering.
AZRAQI:v1p179/r4.anchor: وفيها يقول لبيد بن ربيعة بن جعفر الكلابي

IBNHIBBAN:v8p118/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v8p118/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNHIBBAN:v8p118/r1.claim: Abū Dharr reports the Prophet’s warning against hoarding: he would give away even a mountain of gold, the wealthy will be few on Judgment Day, and monotheists enter Paradise even if they sinned.
IBNHIBBAN:v8p118/r1.anchor: أشهد بالله لسمعت أبا ذر بالربذة يقول: كنت أمشي مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحرة المدينة ممسيا

IBNHIBBAN:v8p118/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v8p118/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNHIBBAN:v8p118/r2.claim: Abū Ḥātim says the promise is conditional: God may pardon a monotheist’s sins before entry, or the person may enter after punishment in Hell; it is not an unconditional guarantee.
IBNHIBBAN:v8p118/r2.anchor: قال أبو حاتم رضي الله تعالى عنه: أضمر في هذا الخبر شرطان: أحدهما: أن من مات لا يشرك بالله شيئا دخل الجنة
